title: Sell Mineral Rights in Loop, TX
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Loop, TX
metaDescription: Loop sits on the western edge of the Midland Basin in Gaines County, an area that's seen steady Wolfcamp and Spraberry horizontal development. We buy interests direct.
heroLead: Loop sits out toward the western edge of Gaines County, close to where the Midland Basin starts giving way to the Central Basin Platform.
intro: Gaines County has seen steady horizontal Wolfcamp and Spraberry development over the last several years, and Loop-area acreage has been part of that, alongside older legacy fields further west and south in the county.

sections.heading: Basin edge means we check both directions
paragraphs: Because Loop sits closer to the basin margin, we look both at classic Midland Basin horizontal activity and at any shallower, older production that might be tied to your specific tract. The geology transitions gradually here rather than at a hard line, so tract-level history matters more than a general county picture.

sections.heading: Rural land, ranching-family ownership
paragraphs: A lot of the mineral interests we see around Loop trace back to ranching families who've held the land for generations. If your interest is part of a larger family holding that's since been split among heirs, we can work with individual shares without needing everyone to agree at once.

sections.heading: Gaines County activity trends
paragraphs: Gaines County has drawn steady horizontal development over recent years, with operators moving across the county in phases rather than all at once. We keep an eye on where current permitting is concentrated so we can give you an accurate read on whether your specific area is in an active phase right now or between rounds of drilling.

faqs.question: Is Loop part of the active Midland Basin horizontal play?
faqs.answer: Much of it is, though sitting near the basin edge means some acreage carries older, shallower production too. We check your specific tract's history before quoting.

faqs.question: My family's Loop-area interest is split among several heirs. Can you buy just my share?
faqs.answer: Yes, we regularly purchase individual fractional interests without requiring the rest of the family to sell alongside you.

faqs.question: What information do you need to start?
faqs.answer: A recent division order or check stub is fastest, but we can also research your interest through Gaines County records if you don't have current paperwork.

faqs.question: Is Gaines County in an active drilling phase right now?
faqs.answer: It varies by area and by year, since operators here tend to develop in phases. We check current permits near your specific tract rather than giving a blanket answer for the whole county.

faqs.question: Do you buy small rural tracts like the ones common around Loop?
faqs.answer: Yes, tract size doesn't disqualify an interest. We evaluate rural acreage the same way we evaluate a larger holding, based on its actual production and permit history.
